open_points.subject: R0-97 refused-attempt counters
open_points.text: Registry counts refused attempts in memory from its start and shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind: refused sign-ins and lockouts
open_points.question: What increments the refused-sign-in and lockout counters: each wrong-or-missing credential, each lockout started, each sign-in refused during a lockout, or some stated combination; and does a successful sign-in clear only A13's throttling state or also the displayed cumulative counter?
options: Count wrong-or-missing credentials and each lockout-start event separately; do not count attempts made during lockout; successful sign-in clears only A13 throttling state.
Count every refused sign-in, including those during lockout, and count each lockout-start event separately.
Reuse A13's refusal count, so successful sign-in clears the displayed refused-sign-in counter.
open_points.default_guess: Use separate cumulative counters since process start: increment refused sign-ins for every refused sign-in, increment lockouts once when each lockout starts, and let successful sign-in clear only A13's throttling window.

witness.initial: Registry has started, has no counters yet, and the owner submits five wrong credentials, one correct credential during lockout, then signs in successfully after the lockout.
events: The owner makes five wrong sign-ins and starts a lockout.
The owner makes one sign-in with the correct credential during the lockout.
After 15 minutes the owner signs in successfully and sees the counters.
outcomes: The page shows six refused sign-ins and one lockout, retained despite the successful sign-in.
The page shows five refused sign-ins and one lockout, or zero refused sign-ins if A13's cleared throttle count was reused.
witness.observer: the owner on the first page after sign-in

open_points.subject: R0-97 counter instants
open_points.text: shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind
open_points.question: Which clock supplies these instants, what UTC representation and precision they have, whether the start instant is read once, and whether one refusal takes one wall-clock reading shared by every counter it updates or separate readings?
options: Use one UTC wall-clock reading at process start and one UTC wall-clock reading per refused request, shared by all counters that request updates.
Read the wall clock separately for each affected counter.
Use monotonic readings internally and derive displayed wall-clock instants.
open_points.default_guess: Use UTC wall-clock instants with time zone and microsecond precision, one reading at process start and one reading per refused request shared by all updates from that request.
consequences: A shared reading makes simultaneous category updates display the same instant and is deterministic.
Separate readings can give different latest instants to counters updated by one request.
Derived wall time can behave differently after wall-clock changes.
open_points.requirement: shows them to the owner on the first page after sign-in, with the instant of the start and of the latest of each kind

open_points.subject: R0-94 retention review qualification
open_points.text: the customers whose relationship ended, and the archived projects archived, longer ago than periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: Are the configured periods exact elapsed durations or calendar periods, what instant or date is compared for each kind, what boundary counts as due, and which period applies when a project and its customer's relationship have different dates?
options: Use calendar periods from the relationship-end date and project archived instant, due at or after the corresponding calendar anniversary.
Use fixed elapsed durations from midnight UTC of the recorded date or from the exact archived instant.
Define one independently configured rule per listed data kind, each with its own anchor and boundary.
open_points.default_guess: Define one configured calendar period per data kind; customers use the recorded relationship-end date, projects use the archived instant, and an item is due at or after the anniversary boundary.
consequences: Calendar and fixed-duration interpretations disagree around leap years and daylight-independent date boundaries.
Using dates versus exact instants changes which items appear during the boundary day.
A single shared period can show an item earlier or later than the governance schedule intended.

open_points.subject: R0-94 retention-period configuration
open_points.text: periods the owner sets in the configuration from the schedule
open_points.question: Which periods must be configured, in what units, and what must Registry do when one is absent, malformed, zero, negative or changed between starts?
options: Require every review period at startup and fail startup on any missing or invalid value.
Allow omitted periods and omit the corresponding kind from the page.
Provide release defaults and let configuration override them.
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit positive period for each reviewed kind and fail startup when any is absent or invalid; changes take effect at the next start.
consequences: Failing startup guarantees the required page cannot silently omit a class but makes configuration mandatory.
Omitting a class can leave due data invisible.
Defaults introduce policy periods not selected by the owner unless the later design declares them.

open_points.subject: R0-96 imported room names and aliases
open_points.text: A room is named by its purpose and, where needed, its number or position — "Bathroom 1", "Kitchen", "Bedroom with balcony" — never by a person, nor by a person's condition, health, disability, age or other need.
open_points.question: Does this writer constraint apply to room names and aliases brought by the one import, and if so must the owner rename every nonconforming imported value before confirmation, or are legacy values admitted unchanged?
options: The import is another owner write and confirmation is unavailable until every imported room name and alias conforms.
The rule applies only to newly entered names; imported legacy values are admitted unchanged.
The mapping must show and allow replacement of every imported room name and alias, but Registry still cannot validate semantic conformity.
open_points.default_guess: Treat import confirmation as an owner write and expose replacements for imported names and aliases, while leaving semantic compliance to the owner rather than Registry validation.

witness.initial: The VPS export contains a picked room named "bathroom for the wheelchair".
events: The owner uploads the export and picks its project.
The owner confirms the mapping without changing that room name.
Registry imports the room and the agent later reads its projection.
outcomes: The import is allowed because A16 checks no semantic room-name rule, and the special-category text reaches the agent.
Confirmation cannot proceed until the owner supplies a compliant replacement, because the import is an owner write governed by R0-96.
witness.observer: the owner during import and the agent reading the imported room

open_points.subject: R0-95 erased values in backups
open_points.text: Registry's backups lose an erased value within the period A18 states.
open_points.question: Is this only A18's conditional guarantee when daily runs and deletions succeed, or is R0-95 requiring an unconditional maximum time after erasure despite A18 allowing failed or missed runs to extend it without a bound?
options: State explicitly that the value disappears within at most 31 days only while the qualifying backup runs succeed, with failures extending the period as A18 says.
Require an unconditional maximum and revise A18 so failed or missed runs cannot leave the value beyond it.
open_points.default_guess: Make the statement conditional on A18's successful-run assumptions and repeat that failures or missed runs extend the period.

witness.initial: A kept backup contains a value that the owner erases from Registry today.
events: Every daily backup run for the next 40 days fails before it can delete old kept backups.
The owner or governance procedure asks whether the erased value can remain in Registry's backups.
outcomes: The value may remain beyond 31 days because A18 says failed runs lengthen the period.
The value must already be gone because R0-95 promises loss within the period A18 states.
witness.observer: the owner conducting the recipient-copy follow-up

open_points.subject: R0-98 cleanup prerequisite
open_points.text: It holds once the owner's earlier machine no longer gives the agent the objects folder (the cleanup step of the home server's move).
open_points.question: Must that cleanup finish before Registry production start or import, or may production and import proceed while the old machine still lets the agent reach the objects folder?
options: Cleanup is a deployment precondition for production start and import.
Production start and import may proceed before cleanup; only the DPIA-screening conclusion waits for cleanup.
Production may start, but the import waits for cleanup.
open_points.default_guess: Require cleanup before the production import, because otherwise the assertion that the move puts the data out of every agent's reach is not yet true.
consequences: Making cleanup a precondition preserves the claimed agent-isolation state at migration time.
Allowing overlap starts production sooner but leaves a period in which the old folder still exposes object photos to the agent.
Separating start from import permits deployment checks before migration while avoiding migration during the exposure.
open_points.requirement: Photos of the objects — homes — do not reach the agent either

open_points.subject: R0-92 Registry-to-Kernel trace correlation
open_points.text: Whether Kernel writes the key it gives as that request id into its trace record, so that a room or pointer leads to exactly one node execution, is Kernel's to state in its case; until it does, the link is one-directional.
open_points.question: Will Kernel's trace record the Registry request id as a correlation key, and if not, what precisely does the claimed one-directional link allow an investigator to find?
options: Kernel records the request id, giving exact bidirectional correlation between a Registry room or pointer and one node execution.
Kernel does not record it; Registry retains its request id but no exact trace lookup is guaranteed.
Kernel records a different correlation key and the cross-service contract defines its mapping to Registry's request id.
open_points.default_guess: Require Kernel to record the same request id so the stated link is operational and exact.
consequences: Recording the same key gives deterministic trace correlation.
Not recording it leaves only approximate correlation by session, action and time and may make the stored key unusable for trace lookup.
A mapped key requires an additional cross-service contract and proof that the mapping is one-to-one.
open_points.requirement: What Registry keeps is the link from its records to that trace: the request id a room's create carries (State 1 M03) and the publisher, with its session, and the request id of a pointer's publish (M05, R0-88).
